entry.title: Weaponizing the Exit: Input Privacy Leakage via Exit Routing Manipulation in Multi-Exit Networks
entry.summary:
Multi-exit networks improve inference efficiency by allowing inputs to terminate early at intermediate exits. We identify a privacy vulnerability in cloud deployments of these networks: a malicious Cloud Service Provider (CSP) can infer sensitive properties of individual user inputs solely from inference latency, without accessing inputs, intermediate states, or model outputs. The attack exploits the CSP's control over the model supply chain.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
entry.summary:
When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #combinatorics

entry.title: Vector Commitment Design, Analysis, and Applications: A Survey
entry.summary:
Due to their widespread applications in decentralized and privacy preserving technologies, commitment schemes have become increasingly important cryptographic primitives. With a wide variety of applications, many new constructions have been proposed, each enjoying different features and security guarantees. In this paper, we systematize the designs, features, properties, and applications of vector commitments (VCs).

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #combinatorics

entry.title: BitVM3: Efficient Bitcoin Bridges via Garbled Circuits
entry.summary:
Bitcoin bridges, protocols that lock BTC on Bitcoin and represent it on a secondary system, underpin much of Bitcoin's application layer, yet remain poorly secured. Deployed bridges rely on federated custody with honest-majority assumptions, while BitVM2, the state of the art in trust-minimized bridging, incurs worst-case dispute costs of approximately $16,000, requiring large operator bonds and deposits that restrict participation to well-capitalized parties. We present BitVM3-BRIDGE, a trust-minimized bridge architecture from Bitcoin to (i) chains with finality certificates, such as Ethereum, and (ii) Bitcoin rollups.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #consensus

entry.title: SoK: Private LLM Inference using Approximate Homomorphic Encryption
entry.summary:
Although recent surveys on privacy-enhancing technologies concluded that FHE cannot feasibly evaluate non-linear activation functions in modern ML architectures, 21 CKKS-based frameworks have since demonstrated end-to-end private inference of LLMs with up to 8B parameters. However, as the field grows rapidly, the literature has become fragmented. Frameworks differ in ciphertext packing layouts, model fidelity, software and hardware stacks, and reported metrics, that hinder direct comparison and reproducibility.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #compilers
